rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are Eisenhower resignation-acceptance letters for senior Cabinet officials, written within weeks of each other, and follow the same unusually close progression: deep regret and acceptance of a departure previously discussed; characterization of the official's responsibilities as especially challenging and complex; praise of effective leadership and institutional accomplishments; prediction of lasting satisfaction or continuing benefit; acknowledgment that Cabinet-level colleagues will miss the official's wise counsel; personal gratitude; and the same warm closing. C07 and C25 share parts of this resignation-letter structure, but their language and sequencing are less closely aligned with the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your departure from the Administration in the near future is a matter of very deep regret to me... when we first discussed your return to private life... I must abide by it and accept your resignation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I deeply regret that the time is rapidly approaching when you will leave Government service. In keeping with the desires you expressed in your letter and in our earlier discussions, I must of course accept your resignation...
shared_material.explanation: Both open with deep regret over an approaching departure, refer to prior discussions, and formally accept the resignation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The goals you undertook to attain... were extremely challenging... your effective leadership... will have continuing effect in the Department's high standards of performance.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the problems... have indeed been challenging... Thanks in large measure to your effective leadership and successful management of very complex responsibilities...
shared_material.explanation: The letters use closely parallel language to frame the office's work as challenging and complex and attribute success to the departing official's effective leadership.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It should long give you cause for pride and great satisfaction.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the continuing readiness of our armed forces will be a lasting satisfaction to you.
shared_material.explanation: Both predict that the enduring institutional results will remain a source of satisfaction to the departing official.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the other members of the Cabinet... will all share a deep sense of loss... For the wise counsel... I shall ever be thankful.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: your associates in the Department, the National Security Council, and the Cabinet... will... greatly miss the wise counsel you have so helpfully provided... I have been deeply and constantly grateful.
shared_material.explanation: Both move from institutional achievement to colleagues' anticipated loss of the official's wise counsel, followed by the President's personal gratitude.
The identical closing is routine by itself, but it reinforces the broader literal and structural correspondence.
